question: How many confirmed 2026 measles cases will Iowa HHS report in its October 1, 2026 update?

calls.reasoning: Resolution is Iowa HHS's own weekly figure; the page reads 38 dated Sep 17, and exactly two further Thursday updates (Sep 24, Oct 1) fall before resolution. Prior from the reference class: statewide counts in undervaccinated-community outbreaks typically grow ~1.35x over a 2-week window at this stage, giving ~51 as the anchor. Adjustments run both ways and roughly offset: downward for five weeks of active response, 'no exposure locations identified in the last four weeks', a small named susceptible pool (Davis County mobile clinic targeting ~280 people), one already-observed zero-growth week, and the likelihood that part of the +16 was retrospective epi-link case-finding (14 of 38 are epi-linked, not lab-confirmed); upward for cases spread across four HHS districts including the Des Moines metro, 22 of 38 in the 5-19 school-age band with school in session, 36 of 38 unvaccinated/unknown, and an adjacent Wisconsin outbreak at 166 and still adding cases. Distribution is right-skewed: the floor is hard (cumulative counts cannot fall, and a two-week total freeze is a live ~7% branch given Sep 10), while the ceiling is open. 70 corresponds precisely to the most recent weekly increment repeating twice, so sustained-or-accelerating growth puts the outcome outside the range - priced at 10%. A small further pull toward the low end comes from the fine print: if Iowa skips the Oct 1 update (~8%), the Sep 24 figure resolves, capturing one increment instead of two. No Iowa-specific prediction market exists; national Polymarket measles contracts do not match on threshold, geography, or resolution source and were not used as an anchor.

- Measles serial interval is ~11-14 days, so roughly one generation fits inside the Sep 17 -> Oct 1 window; cases reported in the Sep 17 batch would be expected to generate their secondaries with rash onset in the Sep 17-Oct 1 range, subject to lab and reporting lag that can push a given case into the following Thursday's batch.

calls.reasoning: Anchor: 38 as of the 9/17 Iowa HHS update (verified live on the page). Two more weekly updates (9/24, 10/1) land before resolution, so the question is a 2-week increment. Reference class of active US state outbreaks ~5 weeks in at ~40 cases gives a median 2-week multiplier of ~1.25 (base ~48), with a fat right tail. Iowa's own recent 2-week factors are 1.375 (Aug 21->Sep 3) and 1.73 (Sep 3->Sep 17), arguing upward; the lumpy pattern (+3, 0, +16) means a single batch of epi-linked reclassifications can move the number a lot in one Thursday. Downward: no new exposure locations in four weeks, active MMR clinics in Davis County since Aug 18, contacts already under quarantine, and small-settlement susceptible pools deplete fast. Measles serial interval ~14 days means generation 4 onsets (~Sep 24-Oct 5) would be only partially reported by the 10/1 update. Non-trivial point mass at exactly 38 (a zero-growth fortnight already occurred the week of Sep 10). Upper bound is open and only ~33 cases away, less than a single recent weekly jump doubled, so I price 10% above 70. No matching market exists; only national US count markets, which I did not blend.

The broad class multiplier is ~1.3x (=49); the narrow Anabaptist class implies ~2x, but Iowa's own realized doubling time is ~5 weeks, not ~1.5, so the narrow class informs the tail rather than the center. calls.reconciliation: Three disputes mattered. (1) Reference class: Runs 1/2 anchored on a broad state-outbreak class (~1.25-1.35x over two weeks) with small adjustments; Run 3 anchored on a narrow Anabaptist class (~2x) then adjusted down hard. Judgment, and I resolved it by precedence of measurement: Iowa has five weeks of its own published series (16 -> 38, increments +3,+3,0,+16), which dominates a class prior for the central estimate; the Anabaptist class is retained only as justification for the fat right tail. I carried forward the runs' shared 38-as-of-Sep-17 anchor and a dispersion close to theirs (25 vs 24-27), recomputed from this outbreak's own increment SD rather than adopted. (2) Whether the +16 posted Sep 17 was genuine incidence or a retrospective batch of epi-linked contacts: FACTUAL, and unsettleable - all three runs searched for an Iowa HHS statement, an epi curve by rash-onset week, and county-level detail, and none exists publicly; no web access on this run to retry. I therefore did not pick a side, and let it widen the distribution symmetrically rather than shift the median. (3) Mass at exactly 38: Run 2's p10=38 implies >=10% on two consecutive zero-growth updates; the Sep 10 zero week supports some mass, but a freeze directly after a +16 week is less likely than an unconditional read suggests, so I put ~5% and set p10=40 - outside Run 2 on the low side and consistent with Runs 1/3. Minor factual check: Runs 1 and 3 both report the Aug 27 figure as 19 from an Iowa HHS release; Run 2's series omits it. Settled as 19; it does not move the estimate. Whether the Davis County epicenter is an Amish settlement was asserted by Runs 2/3 (KCRG Aug 18, mobile vaccination site explicitly open to the Amish community) and flagged unconfirmed by Run 1 - I treat it as likely but not established, which is why the Anabaptist tail is priced at 9% rather than the 14% Run 3 used. Skipped-Oct-1 risk: no run found a holiday or announced cadence change; ~5%, held as a small leftward pull via the fine print. All three found no matching market on Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmakers - only national CDC-counter contracts, which match on neither geography, threshold, deadline nor resolution source - so there is no crowd anchor and none was blended.
